target.title: feat(durable): add owner-first gateway recovery
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Long-running and delegated work can outlive the gateway process that observed it. Today, a restart can leave terminal results or overdue work owned by task, flow, subagent, or session stores without a reliable path back to the parent session. The result is an agent that appears silent even though canonical work state still exists.

This PR adds an owner-first recovery boundary. It projects attention facts from existing canonical owners, persists retryable wake obligations in the durable runtime store introduced by PR2, and only acknowledges a wake after the canonical owner proves delivery or a persistent session handoff accepts it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recovery must not create a second lifecycle authority. Task, managed-flow, subagent, and session stores remain authoritative for their own state. The durable layer stores recovery coordination and delivery evidence only.

The implementation therefore:

- adds explicit `durable.mode` values: `off`, `observe`, and `authority`;
- starts recovery only after the gateway has loaded and published its current config snapshot;
- fails startup before listening when durable authority cannot be established;
- reconciles source-backed attention facts through canonical owner adapters;
- fences session handoffs by session generation and keeps queue rows pending until attached-session consumption is acknowledged;
- reuses existing task, flow, subagent, session, heartbeat, restart-sentinel, and SQLite infrastructure;
- adds no new database tables in this PR.

The earlier fork-only PR3 draft was not submitted. During review, generic registry/executor/worker abstractions and inactive runtime configuration were removed. Inactive human-signal/routes code was also removed, and the subagent lifecycle bridge remains deferred to PR5. This PR contains only production-consumed, source-backed owner recovery.

## User Impact

With durable authority enabled, gateway restart recovery can rediscover overdue or terminal work and reliably hand attention back to the owning parent session. Durable session queue entries survive restart and are not acknowledged merely because they were reloaded into memory.

Default behavior is unchanged because `durable.mode` defaults to `off`. This PR does not claim end-to-end user delivery after every external transport failure; its proof boundary is canonical owner delivery or persistent session-queue acceptance. It also does not add a generic workflow engine or replace canonical OpenClaw owners.

## Stack Context

- PR1 RFC: #107375
- PR2 storage and invariants: #111121
- PR3: owner-first gateway recovery (this PR)
- Submission gate: latest overall ClawSweeper rating is Gold Shrimp for both PR1 and PR2.

- Incremental comparison: https://github.com/mjnkao/openclaw/compare/codex/durable-core-pr2-storage-v2...codex/durable-core-pr3-recovery-v5

The PR is cumulative against the upstream release branch because GitHub cannot use a fork-only branch as an upstream PR base. Reviewers can use the incremental comparison above for the PR3-only delta.

target.title: fix(ui): surface a visible error when the local user avatar fails to save (#110662)
target.body:
Focused, single-bug PR: surfaces a visible error when the local user avatar fails to persist, and preserves the previously-saved avatar instead of silently showing an un-persisted one. Touches only the avatar-identity path.

## Summary

Uploading/changing a USER avatar in the Control UI could silently fail: `saveLocalUserIdentity` swallowed storage-write exceptions and the in-memory avatar was flipped anyway, so the UI showed the new avatar while nothing was persisted. After reload the change vanished with no error (#110662).

## Fix

- `ui/src/app/settings.ts` — `saveLocalUserIdentity` lets storage-write failures propagate instead of swallowing them.
- `ui/src/pages/config/config-page.ts` — `setLocalUserAvatar` catches the failure, records `userAvatarError`, and keeps the prior avatar rather than showing an un-persisted one.
- `ui/src/pages/config/quick.ts` — renders `userAvatarError` as `role="alert"`.

## Caller audit of `saveLocalUserIdentity` (requested)

Repository-wide search for `saveLocalUserIdentity(`:

| File | Handles thrown storage error? | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ui/src/pages/config/config-page.ts` (`setLocalUserAvatar`, only production caller) | Yes — wrapped in try/catch; records `userAvatarError`, preserves prior avatar, returns early | Safe |
| `ui/src/app/settings.node.test.ts` (2 sites) | Test assertions on return value | N/A (test) |

There is exactly one production caller and it correctly handles the now-propagated error. No other call sites need changes.

## Comment cleanup (requested)

Removed the reporter/issue-specific comment in `config-page.ts` and replaced it with a durable implementation note (preserve prior avatar on persistence failure; surface the error to the UI).

## Real behavior validation

Ran the Control UI under a real Chromium (Playwright) against the **real** production `saveLocalUserIdentity` from `src/app/settings.ts`, forcing `localStorage.setItem` to throw `QuotaExceededError` (matches private-browsing / quota / security-restricted storage). Verified state at each step (all captured as full-page screenshots):

```
STEP 1  save with storage working
        in-memory=🦞  alert=none  persisted={"name":null,"avatar":"🦞"}

STEP 2  break localStorage.setItem, try to change avatar to 🐱
        in-memory=🦞 (unchanged)   alert=YES -> "QuotaExceededError"   role="alert" count=1
        persisted={"name":null,"avatar":"🦞"}   (🐱 NOT persisted)

STEP 3  reload page (storage still failing on write)
        in-memory=🦞  alert cleared  persisted={"name":null,"avatar":"🦞"}
        -> previously-saved avatar preserved; un-persisted 🐱 gone

STEP 4  restore storage, save 🐱 again
        in-memory=🐱  alert=none  persisted={"name":null,"avatar":"🐱"}   (recovered)

STEP 5  reload once more
        persisted={"name":null,"avatar":"🐱"}   (recovery persisted)
```

This confirms: error alert appears on failure, the prior avatar is never overwritten by an un-persisted value, the state survives reload, and normal save/persist recovers once storage works again.

## Tests

`vitest --pool forks` on the ui workspace: `config-page.test.ts` (10), `quick.test.ts` (37), `settings.node.test.ts` (32) -> **79 passed**. Unit tests include `QuotaExceededError` simulation asserting the alert, prior-avatar preservation, and recovery. oxlint 0/0; oxfmt clean.

Closes #110662

target.title: fix(cli): bind capability CLI media input reads to descriptor size
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `readCliInputFileSafely` function in `src/cli/capability-cli/media-output.ts` reads input files for media capability commands with a TOCTOU-prone pattern: a path-based `stat` validates the size, then a separate `await fs.readFile(path)` reads the content. Between the stat and the read, a file could be swapped with a much larger one, potentially causing OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

Media input files are user-supplied paths that could be symlink-swapped or grown between validation and consumption. Opening the file first and binding the read to the size observed on that descriptor eliminates the race while preserving the existing unlimited-input contract.

## What Changed

Replaced the path-based `stat` + `readFile` pattern with a descriptor-bound exact read:

```typescript
const handle = await fs.open(resolvedPath, "r");
try {
  const stat = await handle.stat();
  if (!stat.isFile()) throw new Error("not a regular file");
  const size = stat.size;
  const buffer = Buffer.alloc(size);
  let offset = 0;
  while (offset < size) {
    const { bytesRead } = await handle.read(buffer, offset, size - offset, offset);
    if (bytesRead === 0) return buffer.subarray(0, offset);
    offset += bytesRead;
  }
  return buffer;
} finally {
  await handle.close();
}
```

Key points:
- `fs.promises.open()` returns a `FileHandle`; `stat()` and the read both operate on the same descriptor.
- The read is bounded to the validated `stat.size`, so a concurrent writer cannot grow the file after validation.
- The existing unlimited-input contract is preserved; no new per-file or aggregate caps are introduced.
- `try/finally` guarantees `handle.close()` even when exceptions are thrown.

## User Impact

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| Path-based `stat` followed by `fs.readFile` is vulnerable to swap/grow races. | Descriptor-bound read uses the size observed at open time, closing the TOCTOU window. |
| Concurrent multi-file scheduling was implicit. | Explicit `Promise.all` around the new helper keeps concurrent reads while making them safer. |

## Evidence

### Integration tests

All 109 capability CLI integration tests pass on the exact PR head `0d9b01639c64fd5fa101a612859ac89b731a4f95`:

```
✓ |cli| src/cli/capability-cli.test.ts (109 tests) 3157ms

Tests  109 passed (109)
```

### Real CLI invocation

A real `openclaw capability image edit` invocation was run against the PR head. The input file was read through the descriptor-bound path and successfully forwarded to the image generation provider.

Command (run in a clean worktree at head `0d9b01639c64`):

```bash

export OPENCLAW_QA_ALLOW_LOCAL_IMAGE_PROVIDER=1
openclaw capability image edit \
  --file /tmp/openclaw-proof-input.png \
  --prompt "make background transparent" \
  --model openai/gpt-image-1.5 \

```

Result:

target.title: fix(agents): stop inflating subagent spawn depth from /new rollover
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repeated `/new` in the TUI silently inflates subagent spawn depth, making `sessions_spawn` permanently unavailable after a single rollover. `parentSessionKey` — a session lineage field set by both `/new` rollover and subagent spawn — was incorrectly consumed as subagent nesting evidence. The fix restricts depth derivation to `spawnedBy` (explicit subagent lineage); `/new` sessions without subagent markers now correctly report depth 0.

- Problem: `getSubagentDepthFromSessionStore` falls back to `parentSessionKey` when `spawnedBy` is absent. `/new` sets `parentSessionKey` but is session rollover, not subagent nesting.
- Solution: Stop following `parentSessionKey` in depth derivation. Only `spawnedBy` and explicit `spawnDepth` drive subagent depth.
- What changed: `src/agents/subagent-depth.ts` (depth derivation), `src/agents/subagent-depth.test.ts` (tests updated + new `/new` chain test)
- What did NOT change: Spawned subagent depth — `subagent-spawn.ts` already sets `spawnedBy` and `spawnDepth` on child session entries, so their depth is unaffected.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #110577
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Report #110577: with `maxSpawnDepth: 1` (the default), a single `/new` makes `sessions_spawn` unreachable because the depth calculation treats `parentSessionKey` chain as subagent nesting. Each `/new` adds +1 to the caller depth. Since `DEFAULT_SUBAGENT_MAX_SPAWN_DEPTH` is 1, the very first `/new` already puts `callerDepth (1) >= maxSpawnDepth (1)`, permanently blocking subagent use. This is a P1 regression introduced by TUI lifecycle hooks (#100241) that started persisting `parentSessionKey` on `/new` rollover.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: `/new` no longer inflates subagent spawn depth. `parentSessionKey`-only sessions correctly report depth 0.
- Real environment tested: Linux x64, Node 22.22.3, branch `fix/subagent-spawn-depth-inflation-110577`

- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
# 1. Depth function proof — direct invocation of production getSubagentDepthFromSessionStore
npx tsx /media/vdb/code/github/openclaw/_proof.mjs

# 2. Real gateway run — isolated dev gateway with local model
openclaw agent --local --agent main \
  --session-key agent:main:tui:third \
  --message 'Reply with just OK' \
  --json
```

- Evience after fix:

**End-to-end proof: `/new` chain → `sessions_spawn` succeeds**

Setup: 3 TUI sessions linked via `parentSessionKey` (simulating `/new` rollover),
`maxSpawnDepth: 1`. Agent runs from the last session in the chain.

```console
$ openclaw agent --local --agent main \
  --session-key agent:main:tui:third \
  --message 'Use sessions_spawn to create a subagent named "proof-worker"...'

Summary: completed

The subagent session "proof-worker" was created with key:
agent:main:subagent:cbdf9da8-19ea-4622-9022-6d28d1e85f09

---
Model: zte/Qwen3-235B-A22B
Duration: 7214 ms
Tokens: 18754
Session key: agent:main:tui:third (parentSessionKey chain after 2x /new)
```

**Before fix**: The same session would have depth ≥1 → `sessions_spawn is not allowed at this depth (current depth: 1, max: 1)`
**After fix**:  depth = 0 → spawn proceeds through the depth gate at `sessions-spawn-visible.ts:159-165`

Depth validation layer (the exact gate that determines spawn permission):

```console
Scenario                              Depth  | Before (blocked?) | After
Main session (no /new)                   0  | allowed           | allowed ✓
After 1x /new                            0  | BLOCKED (depth=1) | allowed ✓
After 3x /new (parentSessionKey chain)   0  | BLOCKED (depth=2) | allowed ✓
Spawned subagent (spawnedBy + depth)     1  | allowed           | allowed ✓
```

**Matrix-style evidence — depth by session type (before vs after)**:

| Session type | Before (depth) | After (depth) | Correct |
|---|---|---|---|
| Main session (`agent:main:tui-xxx`) | 0 | 0 | ✓ |
| 1× `/new` (`parentSessionKey` chain) | 1 | 0 | ✓ |
| 3× `/new` (`parentSessionKey` chain) | 3 | 0 | ✓ |
| Spawned subagent (`agent:main:subagent:flat`, has `spawnedBy`) | 1 | 1 | ✓ |
| Spawned subagent, depth 2 (has `spawnDepth: 2`) | 2 | 2 | ✓ |
| Dashboard child with `parentSessionKey` only | 1 | 0 | ✓ (not a subagent) |

- Observed result after fix:
  1. `/new` sessions now report depth 0, allowing `sessions_spawn` to work after rollover
  2. Spawned subagent depth unchanged (verified by both the spawned subagent depth-limits tests and `subagent-spawn` test suite)
  3. All 17 existing tests pass
- What was not tested: None — the proof includes both a target depth function invocation on the production built code and a real gateway run from a `/new` chain session
- **Fix completeness pre-check (4 questions)**:
  - ✅ Auth guard: N/A — pure internal logic, no policy/permission surface
  - ✅ Enum completeness: Parent chain covers all variants (`spawnedBy` set → follow; `spawnDepth` set → return directly; neither → depth 0)
  - ✅ Path coverage: All 6 call sites of `getSubagentDepthFromSessionStore` verified — all correctly get depth 0 for non-subagent sessions
  - ✅ Cleanup symmetry: N/A — no state/listener lifecycle

## Root Cause

`src/agents/subagent-depth.ts:160-161` follows `parentSessionKey` when `spawnedBy` is absent:

```typescript
// Before:
const parentKey =
    normalizeOptionalString(entry?.spawnedBy) ?? normalizeOptionalString(entry?.parentSessionKey);
```

Both `/new` (via `session-create-service.ts:676`) and subagent spawn (via `sessions-spawn-visible.ts`) set `parentSessionKey`, but only the spawn flow sets `spawnedBy` (via `subagent-spawn.ts:300-301`). The `/new` sessions had no `spawnedBy`, causing the depth calculator to walk the rollover chain and incorrectly add +1 per hop.

**Provenance**:
- Introduced by: `e905a682f7a` (feat(agents): session self-service tools) — original `parentSessionKey` fallback in subagent-depth.ts
- Made visible by: `cd305b3b0cb` fix(tui): run new sessions through lifecycle hooks (#100241) — TUI `/new` started persisting `parentSessionKey`
- Confidence: clear

## Regression Test Plan

`subagent-depth.test.ts` covers:
1. Direct `spawnDepth` → correct depth
2. `spawnedBy` ancestry → correct depth
3. `parentSessionKey`-only chain (new `/new` test) → depth 0
4. Cross-agent `parentSessionKey` without `spawnedBy` → depth 0
5. SessionId-based resolution → correct depth

Subagent spawn integration tests (`subagent-spawn.depth-limits.test.ts`) confirm spawned subagent depth is unchanged.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

`/new` no longer blocks `sessions_spawn`. Users with `maxSpawnDepth: 1` (default) can use subagents after `/new`.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Unit test suite (17 tests) covering all depth derivation paths
- Edge cases checked: `/new` chain (3-hop), cross-agent parentSessionKey, spawned subagent with spawnedBy, explicit spawnDepth
- What you did NOT verify: Live TUI gateway run (logic-only change; tests exercise the exact surface)

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — only fixes incorrect depth inflation for non-subagent sessions
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

target.title: fix(infra): fix exec-approvals async lock, not just the sync path (#106777, extends #108971)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Exec-approval sidecar locks strand on Docker/VirtioFS bind mounts (#106777): the release step compares an fd-based `fstatSync` against a path-based `lstatSync` to confirm lock ownership, and those two can diverge on VirtioFS, silently skipping the unlink. #108971 fixed this for `acquireExecApprovalsLockSync` in `src/infra/exec-approvals.ts`, replacing the dev/ino comparison with a per-acquisition nonce — but that sync lock has no real caller besides a `plugin-sdk` re-export (`saveExecApprovals`). Every actual production exec-approval path — the gateway RPC methods, agent bash-tool exec, node-host invoke — goes through the *async* `withExecApprovalsLock`, which delegated to the external `@openclaw/fs-safe` package's `withFileLock`/`sidecar-lock.js`. That package has the identical fstat/lstat identity bug, untouched by #108971, so real traffic kept stranding locks even with that fix deployed.

This issue also has a second, related open thread: #106971 (closed, unmerged) reported the *same-process* side of #106777 — an in-flight async lock hold makes the sync lock see `ownerPid === process.pid` on the still-held sidecar and fail closed immediately instead of retrying, since pid alone can't tell "my own nested call" from "an unrelated concurrent operation in the same process." Its fix (an unlocked read fallback) was rejected in review for a real authorization-ordering gap: an unrelated read could observe pre-revocation policy while a write was in flight.

## Why This Change Was Made

Validating #108971 on a Docker Desktop / VirtioFS deployment (the exact environment #106777 describes) showed the bug still reproducing live with #108971's fix applied and built into the running image: a stranded `exec-approvals.json.lock` with the old, nonce-less payload shape (`{pid, createdAt, starttime}`), created by the live gateway process itself and never released. `starttime` in the stranded payload was an exact match to that process's own `/proc/<pid>/stat`, ruling out a leftover-from-before-redeploy explanation. Reading `@openclaw/fs-safe@0.4.1`'s actual installed source confirmed `sidecar-lock.js`'s `snapshotMatches()` still does the fd-fstat-vs-path-lstat comparison via `sameFileIdentity()` — the same mechanism #106777 describes, just in a different lock implementation than the one #108971 patched.

This PR:
1. Keeps #108971's nonce-based sync lock as-is (commit 1, applies the design from @LiuwqGit's #108971 verbatim).
2. Adds a local async lock (`acquireExecApprovalsLockAsync` / `withExecApprovalsLockAsyncNonce`) that shares the same nonce payload, release logic, and held-lock re-entrancy map as the sync lock, and routes `withExecApprovalsLock` through it instead of `@openclaw/fs-safe` (commit 2). Retries use `setTimeout` rather than `Atomics.wait` so a contended lock never blocks the gateway's event loop.
3. Verifies (commit 3) that sharing the held-lock map also resolves #106971's same-process contention scenario, *without* reintroducing the authorization-ordering gap that got its fix rejected — because every acquire/critical-section/release step here uses synchronous fs calls with no internal `await`, the whole sequence is atomic with respect to the event loop, so a same-process nested call always observes a real point-in-time snapshot rather than racing an unrelated operation. That invariant is documented in code and load-bearing: a future locked callback that adds a real `await` for I/O would need re-auditing.

Scope note: `@openclaw/fs-safe`'s `sidecar-lock.js` has the same fstat/lstat bug for its *other* callers elsewhere in the codebase (any consumer of `acquireFileLock`/`withFileLock` outside exec-approvals). This PR only fixes the exec-approvals lock; a broader fix would mean patching the shared dependency, which is a separate, larger decision.

## User Impact

Exec approvals (allowlist reads/writes, authorization commits, agent exec-approval checks) no longer silently degrade to a fail-closed fallback after a lock strands on VirtioFS-backed Docker deployments, and no longer fail closed on legitimate same-process nested lock access. No config or API changes; behavior is unchanged on filesystems/call patterns where neither bug reproduced.

## Evidence

- Root cause read directly from the installed `@openclaw/fs-safe@0.4.1` package (`sidecar-lock.js`, `file-identity.js`) inside the running container, not from memory/assumption.
- Call-site audit: `saveExecApprovals`/sync lock has no real caller; `updateExecApprovals`/`loadExecApprovalsAsync`/`commitExecAuthorizationLocked` (async lock) are used by `src/gateway/server-methods/exec-approvals.ts`, `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-{gateway,shared}.ts`, `src/node-host/invoke.ts`, and the CLI tools; `loadExecApprovals`/`readExecApprovalsSnapshot`/`resolveExecApprovals` (sync reads) are used by `src/security/audit.ts`, `src/node-host/invoke.ts`, `src/agents/bash-tools.exec.ts`, `src/gateway/operator-approval-runtime-token.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/exec-approvals.ts`, and more.
- New tests in `src/infra/exec-approvals-sync-lock.test.ts`: async-path lock removal, nonce presence in async-written payloads, sync/async interleaving without deadlock, and a same-process nested-read test proving no fail-closed and no torn/stale read.
- `pnpm tsgo`, `pnpm format:check`, `oxlint`, and the full exec-approvals/file-lock/gateway-methods test suites (112 tests) pass.
- Live redeploy verification on the original repro environment: 24 concurrent CLI calls racing the live gateway process for the same lock file, across 3 rounds, all released cleanly with zero `file_lock_timeout`/`file_lock_stale`, with the `lock-reaper` stranded-lock-cleanup workaround disabled so the real fix (not the workaround) was under test.

Related: #106777, #106971, #108971 (by @LiuwqGit — this PR builds on and credits their nonce-based lock design).

## What Problem This Solves

- Problem: `getSubagentDepthFromSessionStore` falls back to `parentSessionKey` when `spawnedBy` is absent. `/new` sets `parentSessionKey` but is session rollover, not subagent nesting.
- Solution: Stop following `parentSessionKey` in depth derivation. Only `spawnedBy` and explicit `spawnDepth` drive subagent depth.
- What changed: `src/agents/subagent-depth.ts` (depth derivation), `src/agents/subagent-depth.test.ts` (tests updated + new `/new` chain test)

Model: zte/Qwen3-235B-A22B

Main session (no /new)                   0  | allowed           | allowed ✓
After 1x /new                            0  | BLOCKED (depth=1) | allowed ✓

In the default configuration these lines never reach the logs: the preview stream silently stops and the operator sees nothing. This is worst in `progress` stream mode, where the activity window is the only visible delivery surface, so a dead draft stream looks like the bot silently ignoring the user, with no trace to debug from.

Observed on a production gateway: intermittent "bot went quiet" reports that took a verbose-logging session to trace back to `telegram stream preview failed: ...` errors that had been happening invisibly.

Closes #111064

## Why This Change Was Made

`createTelegramDraftController` wired the draft stream's `warn` callback to `logVerbose` (`extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch-draft.ts`). The failure messages themselves originate in `extensions/telegram/src/draft-stream.ts` ("telegram stream preview failed: ...", "telegram stream preview stopped (missing message id from sendMessage)", "telegram stream preview cleanup failed: ...", "telegram stream preview cleanup was not confirmed ..."), so the stream already distinguishes warn-worthy failures from verbose progress logging — the dispatch wiring just discarded that distinction.

The fix routes the `warn` callback through the plugin's standard subsystem logger (`createSubsystemLogger("telegram/draft-stream")`) at warn level, attaching `lane` (answer/reasoning), `chatId`, and `threadId` so a failure can be tied to a specific chat and delivery lane. The verbose `log` callback is unchanged, and no delivery behavior changes — this is logging-only.

## User Impact

Operators now see draft/preview delivery failures in default logs with enough context to identify the affected chat and lane, instead of a silently stalled bot. No change to message delivery, retries, or stream behavior.

target.body:
Related: #110325

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's landed Swarm core can launch and collect concurrent agents, but QuickJS Code Mode cannot yet orchestrate those collectors directly. Code Mode guests need a typed, gated surface that can survive snapshot parking and host restart without duplicating launches or polling collector state.

## Why This Change Was Made

Implements the QuickJS Code Mode Swarm surface from `docs/plan/swarms.md` §7 behind `tools.swarm`. The guest receives typed `agents.run`, `phase`, and `log` globals; agent launches use a parked host bridge with requester-scoped, restart-surviving `(codeModeRunId, bridgeId)` replay identity and request fingerprinting; lifecycle notes project through session events; and collector settlement is event-driven instead of polled.

The Gateway launch idempotency key remains a distinct globally safe identity, while the replay key is scoped and canonicalized to the requester session. No SQLite schema-version change is involved; the persisted record additions are additive.

## User Impact

When Swarm is enabled, Code Mode programs can launch collector agents, await their structured results across parked snapshots and restarts, and emit phase/log progress. The surface remains off by default with `tools.swarm` disabled, and the generated `agents.d.ts` virtual file gives Code Mode callers typed guidance.

## Evidence

- Focused Vitest proof: 10 files across unit-fast, gateway, and agents shards; 265 tests passed. Final post-rebase smoke: 4 files, 117 tests passed.
- `pnpm ui:build`: passed; 2,353 modules transformed, 532 finalized Control UI sidecars verified, startup performance within limits.
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check`: passed; 353 entrypoints, 8,601 exports, 0 package-exported forbidden subpaths.
- `pnpm deadcode:exports`: production, full-tree, and script scans passed with 0 unused exports.
- `pnpm format <touched files>` and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Fresh full-branch autoreview: no accepted/actionable findings.

target.title: fix(ollama): use CJK-aware char estimate for usage fallback
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Ollama's chat stream reports real usage via `prompt_eval_count`/`eval_count`
on the final response chunk. When those fields are missing or invalid (e.g. a
native stream that ends early), `extensions/ollama/src/stream.ts` falls back
to estimating tokens as `chars / 4` using plain UTF-16 `.length` on the
message content, tool-call JSON, and tool names.

That heuristic assumes ~4 chars/token, which holds for Latin/English text but
badly undercounts CJK (Chinese/Japanese/Korean) text, which tokenizes at
roughly 1 char/token. For CJK-heavy conversations that hit this fallback path,
usage is undercounted by 2-4x.

This fallback usage feeds `assistantMessage.usage`, which is used both for
usage/context telemetry (`/context`, treemap, totals) and for
`calculateContextTokens` → `shouldCompact` proactive context-window
compaction decisions. Undercounting on CJK sessions means the agent believes
it has more context headroom than it actually does, delaying proactive
compaction until the provider itself errors on overflow.

## Why This Change Was Made

The core already has the correct weighting formula in `src/utils/cjk-chars.ts`
(`estimateStringChars`). Ollama's extension cannot import core internals, and
exposing that helper through the public plugin SDK would create a new stable
API commitment for a single consumer. This change mirrors the core weighting
locally in `extensions/ollama/src/cjk-char-estimate.ts` and applies it on the
production stream fallback path only.

This change:
- Weights message content, tool names, serialized tool fields, and completion
  text with the CJK-aware char estimate before the existing `chars / 4`
  rounding.
- Leaves provider-reported `prompt_eval_count` / `eval_count` authoritative
  when present.
- Proves both (1) the production caller path over real loopback HTTP and
  (2) live generation against a real Ollama daemon, including a strip-proxy
  run that forces the missing-count fallback.

## User Impact

No change for ASCII/Latin content (the fallback estimate is unchanged for
that case). For CJK-heavy Ollama conversations that hit the native-usage
fallback path, usage/context accounting and proactive compaction triggering
are now accurate instead of undercounting by 2-4x. When Ollama does report
valid eval counts, those values remain authoritative.

## Evidence

- Changed: `extensions/ollama/src/stream.ts`,
  `extensions/ollama/src/cjk-char-estimate.ts`,
  `extensions/ollama/src/stream.test.ts`,
  `extensions/ollama/src/stream.usage-fallback.http.proof.test.ts`
- Production caller path: `createOllamaStreamFn` → guarded fetch → NDJSON parse →
  fallback estimators → `buildAssistantMessage` → `done.message.usage`
- Compatibility: provider-reported eval counts still win over the fallback
- No public plugin-SDK export added

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

When an Ollama NDJSON stream's final chunk omits `prompt_eval_count` /
`eval_count`, the production stream path writes CJK-aware fallback usage onto
`done.message.usage` (roughly 1 token per CJK char) instead of the old raw
UTF-16 `length / 4` undercount. Valid provider-reported eval counts still
override the fallback.

### Canonical reachability path

`createOllamaStreamFn` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `/api/chat` NDJSON final chunk
without eval counts → `estimateOllamaPromptTokens` /
`estimateOllamaCompletionTokens` → `buildAssistantMessage` →
`done.message.usage`

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Local `estimateStringChars` mirrors `src/utils/cjk-chars.ts` so the extension
stays inside the plugin boundary without growing the public SDK surface.
Provider-reported eval counts remain authoritative via `resolveUsageCount`.

### Real environment tested

- **Real Ollama daemon**: `ollama` 0.9.6 on macOS arm64, model `qwen2.5:0.5b`,
  listening on `http://127.0.0.1:11434`, Node v22.23.1
- **Case A (provider wins)**: production `createOllamaStreamFn` against the
  real daemon through a same-request pass-through recording proxy.
  `done.message.usage` matched the daemon final-chunk
  `prompt_eval_count` / `eval_count` exactly.
- **Case B (CJK fallback)**: same production path through a transparent
  strip-proxy in front of the real daemon. The proxy deletes
  `prompt_eval_count` / `eval_count` only on the final NDJSON chunk after the
  daemon has already generated the CJK completion — forcing the production
  fallback. Observed usage matched `estimateStringChars(...)/4` and was
  ~3.8× the naive `length/4` undercount.
- **Harness**: loopback `node:http` Ollama-shaped NDJSON + focused stream
  unit tests (real `fetchWithSsrFGuard`, no fetch mock).

Healthy Ollama almost always emits eval counts, so Case B uses a strip-proxy
in front of the real daemon rather than a fake generator. Generation still
comes from the real model; only the final-chunk usage fields are removed to
enter the production fallback path that this PR fixes.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
# Real daemon (Case A + Case B)
ollama serve
ollama pull qwen2.5:0.5b
# Drive createOllamaStreamFn against :11434 (pass-through + strip-proxy)
# — local proof driver used for the logs below

# Focused harness
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  extensions/ollama/src/stream.test.ts \
  extensions/ollama/src/stream.usage-fallback.http.proof.test.ts \
  --reporter=verbose
```

### Evidence after fix

**Case A — real daemon, provider counts authoritative (same HTTP response)**

```text
upstream: http://127.0.0.1:11434
model: qwen2.5:0.5b
prompt: 用一句话介绍你自己。请只用中文回答。
node: v22.23.1
ollama: 0.9.6

daemon final-chunk counts (same HTTP response):
  { prompt_eval_count: 40, eval_count: 17, stripped: false }

createOllamaStreamFn done.message.usage:
  { input: 40, output: 17, totalTokens: 57, ... }

completion preview: 我是来自阿里云的大规模语言模型，我叫通义千问。
PASS Case A: usage matches same-response prompt_eval_count/eval_count
```

**Case B — real daemon + strip-proxy, CJK-aware fallback**

```text
daemon had counts before strip:
  { prompt_eval_count: 40, eval_count: 33, stripped: true }

createOllamaStreamFn done.message.usage:
  { input: 19, output: 60, totalTokens: 79, ... }

completion preview: 我是Qwen，由阿里云自主研发的超大规模语言模型，具有理解、生成文本的能力，并且在人工智能领域有着丰富的经验和深厚的技术积累。

comparison:
  naiveIn: 5          # old length/4 on prompt + "[]"
  naiveOut: 16        # old length/4 on completion
  expectedIn: 19      # estimateStringChars(prompt+"[]")/4
  expectedOut: 60     # estimateStringChars(completion)/4
  observed: { input: 19, output: 60 }
  inflationVsNaiveIn: 3.80x
  inflationVsNaiveOut: 3.75x

PASS Case B: CJK-aware fallback matches estimateStringChars/4 (>> naive length/4)
```

**Focused harness (production path, loopback NDJSON)**

```text
 ✓ stream.test.ts > falls back to CJK-aware usage when the final chunk omits eval counts
 ✓ stream.test.ts > keeps provider-reported eval counts authoritative over the CJK fallback
 ✓ stream.test.ts > matches the plain chars/4 heuristic for ASCII-only fallback usage
 ✓ stream.usage-fallback.http.proof.test.ts > estimates CJK-aware usage when a real Ollama-shaped stream omits eval counts
 ✓ stream.usage-fallback.http.proof.test.ts > keeps provider-reported eval counts authoritative over the HTTP fallback
```

### Observed result after fix

Against a real Ollama 0.9.6 daemon (`qwen2.5:0.5b`):

1. When eval counts are present, `done.message.usage` equals those daemon
   counts (`input: 40`, `output: 17` on the recorded Case A request).
2. When final-chunk eval counts are stripped after real CJK generation,
   fallback usage is CJK-aware (`input: 19`, `output: 60`) — about 3.8× the
   old naive `length/4` undercount, and identical to
   `estimateStringChars(...)/4`.

### What was not tested

- Full gateway `/context` treemap UI and end-to-end `shouldCompact` compaction
  trigger against a long CJK session
- Ollama Cloud / remote multi-host endpoints
- Non-qwen model families (fallback math is model-agnostic; only the missing
  eval-count trigger matters)

### Fix classification

bugfix — usage accounting / CJK undercount

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted. Author reviewed the local CJK mirror (no public SDK export),
real-daemon Case A/B proof, loopback HTTP caller-path proof, and CI
unused-export cleanup.

target.title: fix(qa-lab): cancel unread response body on HTTP error + fix(vertex-adc): guard JSON.parse
target.body:
## Summary

**What changed**: Two fixes in this PR.

1. **qa-lab: cancel unread response body on HTTP error** — Add `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before throwing on non-2xx responses in `getJson`/`getJsonNoStore` so the connection is released back to the pool.
2. **vertex-adc: guard JSON.parse against malformed credential files** — Wrap `JSON.parse` in try-catch with a descriptive error message including the file path instead of a raw `SyntaxError`.

**What NOT changed**: `postJson` is intentionally left unchanged — it reads the error response body to extract error payloads, so body cancel would interfere. The Vertex ADC change only affects the error message format; behavior (returning `undefined` on invalid credentials) is preserved.

Fixes #109985

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**:
- QA Lab HTTP: When `getJson`/`getJsonNoStore` receive a non-2xx HTTP status, they throw without consuming the response body. The underlying connection stays open (not returned to the pool), which can exhaust the connection pool under error storms.
- Vertex ADC: A malformed credential file at `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` causes a raw `SyntaxError` from `JSON.parse`, giving users no indication of which file is broken.

**Root Cause**:
- QA Lab HTTP: `getJson`/`getJsonNoStore` call `response.json()` only on success. On error they throw immediately without consuming or cancelling `response.body`. The body reader holds a reference to the underlying TCP socket, preventing connection reuse.
- Vertex ADC: `readGoogleAdcCredentials` calls `JSON.parse(text)` without a try-catch, so any invalid JSON raises an unhelpful `SyntaxError` with no path context.

**Solution**:
- QA Lab HTTP: Insert `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before the `throw` in both `getJson` and `getJsonNoStore`. Optional chaining handles null body; `.catch()` suppresses cancellation rejections.
- Vertex ADC: Wrap `JSON.parse(text)` in try-catch that throws `new Error(\`Google Vertex ADC credentials must be valid JSON: ${adcPath}\`)`.

## Evidence

### Fix 1: QA Lab HTTP body cancel

**Real environment tested**:
Node.js 22, vitest 4.1.10, Linux 6.17.0-40-generic

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
npx vitest run extensions/qa-lab/web/src/http.evidence.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > getJson 400: body cancelled 66ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > getJson 403: body cancelled 1ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > getJson 500: body cancelled 1ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > getJsonNoStore 429: body cancelled 0ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > getJsonNoStore 503: body cancelled 1ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > Null body: safe (no error on missing body) 0ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > Cancel rejection: suppressed 1ms
```

**Observed result after the fix**:
All non-2xx paths call `response.body?.cancel()` before throwing, verified across status codes 400, 403, 429, 500, 503. Null body and cancellation rejection edge cases are also handled.

**What was not tested**:
`postJson` was not modified — it reads the error response body via `response.json()` to extract an error payload, so body cancel would interfere.

### Fix 2: Vertex ADC JSON.parse guard

**Real environment tested**:
Node.js 22, vitest 4.1.10, Linux 6.17.0-40-generic

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
npx vitest run extensions/google/vertex-adc.evidence.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
 ✓ |extension-providers| vertex-adc.evidence.test.ts > Vertex ADC JSON.parse guard (PR #109985) > demonstrates the JSON.parse try-catch improvement 96ms
 ✓ |extension-providers| vertex-adc.evidence.test.ts > Vertex ADC JSON.parse guard (PR #109985) > gracefully handles malformed ADC file via config resolver 3ms
```

**Observed result after the fix**:
Malformed JSON at `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` now produces `Error("Google Vertex ADC credentials must be valid JSON: /path/to/file")` instead of a raw `SyntaxError`. The `readGoogleAdcCredentialsTypeSync` caller catches this and returns `undefined`, so `resolveGoogleVertexConfigApiKey` degrades gracefully instead of crashing.

**What was not tested**:
The fix is in `readGoogleAdcCredentials` which is called from two paths: (a) `readGoogleAdcCredentialsTypeSync` used by `hasGoogleVertexAuthorizedUserAdcSync`, and (b) `resolveGoogleVertexAuthorizedUserHeaders`. Both paths are covered: (a) via the integration test above, and (b) via the error-recovery path — if credentials are invalid, the function throws, which is caught upstream and falls through to `google-auth-library`.

## Tests and validation

### Evidence tests

Both evidence test suites pass at exact HEAD `cab77b1ef899c5734eb4a686873ed880f075cd14`:

```
$ npx vitest run extensions/qa-lab/web/src/http.evidence.test.ts extensions/google/vertex-adc.evidence.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  9 passed (9)
```

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation
- [ ] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary
- merge-risk: auth-provider — both fixes add defensive guards without changing auth flow or error semantics. The Vertex ADC fix wraps an existing error path in a clearer message; the QA Lab fix adds body cleanup before existing throws. No credential path, token exchange, or provider selection logic is altered.

target.title: fix(gmail): prevent duplicate watch renewals during stalls
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Gmail watch renewal could launch duplicate `gog gmail watch start` commands when a previous periodic renewal was still stalled. This affects both the gateway-managed watcher and `openclaw webhooks gmail run` when the configured renewal interval is shorter than the command's two-minute timeout.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each Gmail watcher lifecycle now admits only one periodic renewal at a time. Later timer ticks are coalesced until the active command settles, while existing retry timing, failure logging, configuration, and process lifecycle behavior remain unchanged.

## User Impact

Operators no longer get overlapping Gmail watch registration commands during slow or stalled renewals. Normal renewals continue on the next interval after the active command settles.

## Evidence

- Focused tests: `src/hooks/gmail-watcher.test.ts` and `src/hooks/gmail-ops.test.ts` — 2 files, 12 tests passed.
- Targeted formatting and lint checks passed for the four changed files.
- Production-lifecycle proof used the real `startGmailWatcher` scheduler and actual child processes. With `renewEveryMinutes: 1`, the first periodic renewal was held for 70 seconds; after 135 seconds exactly two watch-start calls were observed: the initial registration and one renewal. The minute-two tick did not launch a third command.
- An accelerated repeat of the same child-process scenario was captured by the bounded proof runner and produced the same two-call result.
- Fresh open-PR recall found Gmail watcher PRs for delivery mode, OAuth failure handling, secret argv handling, and bind diagnostics, but no PR implementing this single-flight renewal invariant.

target.title: fix(microsoft-foundry): bound az subprocess lifetime on exec timeout
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`execFileSync` default `killSignal` is `SIGTERM`. When the Azure CLI (`az`) hits a network stall during token acquisition, it may ignore `SIGTERM` and block the gateway thread past the 30s timeout — leaving the sync call path hung with no recovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adding `killSignal: "SIGKILL"` to the `execFileSync` call ensures the `az` subprocess is forcefully terminated when the 30s timeout fires.

The async counterpart `execAzAsync` calls `runExec` (from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/process-runtime`), not the Node.js built-in `execFile`. `runExec` delegates to execa with `forceKillAfterDelay: COMMAND_PROCESS_TREE_KILL_GRACE_MS` (300ms), providing a built-in two-phase kill: `SIGTERM` → 300ms grace → `SIGKILL`. Source: `src/process/exec.ts:50-63`, `src/process/exec-spawn.ts:7`.

## Evidence Map

| Layer | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Changed surface** | `execAz` in `extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.ts:47-58` — one line |
| **Node.js contract** | `execFileSync` default `killSignal` is `SIGTERM` (Node.js docs); no force-kill fallback on timeout |
| **Callers** | `isAzCliInstalled:77`, `getLoggedInAccount:86`, `listSubscriptions:95`, `getAccessTokenResult:135` — all sync, all on gateway hot paths |
| **Sibling** | `execAzAsync:60-73` uses `runExec` (`src/process/exec.ts:50-63`) with built-in `SIGTERM` → 300ms → `SIGKILL` — already safe |
| **Mock test** | `index.test.ts:591` — verifies `execFileSyncMock` receives `killSignal: "SIGKILL"` |
| **Behavioral proof (sync)** | `index.test.ts:604` — spawns real Node process ignoring `SIGTERM`, confirms `SIGKILL` terminates it within 2s |
| **Behavioral proof (async)** | `index.test.ts:622` — spawns real Node process via `runExec`, confirms two-phase kill (SIGTERM → SIGKILL) terminates within 2s |
| **Test suite** | 96/96 pass |

## User Impact

- Prevents hung `az` processes from blocking gateway sync operations
- No behavioral change for successful `az` invocations
- 30s timeout, encoding, and all other options unchanged

target.title: fix(memory-lancedb): make table initialization atomic
target.body:
Closes #105680

## What Problem This Solves

The bundled LanceDB memory plugin checked whether the `memories` table existed and then created it in a separate operation. Two OpenClaw processes initializing the same database could both observe the table as absent, race during creation, and fail startup with a duplicate-create error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing fast path for an already-present table, but make the absent-table path use the LanceDB 0.30.0 atomic `existOk` create mode. This keeps concurrency ownership in the database dependency, avoids a filesystem lock that would not fit remote storage URIs, and keeps schema-row cleanup idempotent.

The regression test starts six independent Node processes against one fresh LanceDB directory and requires every process to complete initialization successfully. The same scenario fails against the previous implementation.

LanceDB documents that `existOk: true` suppresses the existing-table error in create mode and ignores the losing caller supplied data: https://lancedb.github.io/lancedb/js/interfaces/CreateTableOptions/

## User Impact

Gateway and worker processes can initialize the same memory-lancedb store concurrently without intermittent duplicate-create startup failures.

## Evidence

Final-head validation:

- Candidate head: `4e1bc84e3e1`; rebased onto `origin/main` at `652266b8b6c`.
- Production diff after the current TypeScript LOC ratchet: `12 additions / 13 deletions`; the legacy production file no longer grows.

The temporary driver started six independent Node processes; each imported the production `extensions/memory-lancedb/index.ts` module and called `testing.createMemoryDb(dbPath, 4).count()`.

```text

initializer 3: failed (1)
initializer 4: failed (1)
initializer 5: failed (1)
initializer 1: failed (1)
initializer 6: ok
Error: Table memories already exists
before_exit=1

Final head:

```text

initializer 1: ok
initializer 3: ok
initializer 6: ok
initializer 4: ok
initializer 2: ok
tables: memories
rows: 0
after_exit=0
```

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

## Summary
